questions.question: In March 2025, Operation Brahma was launched to assist earthquake hit __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was launched in **March 2025** by the Government of India to assist Myanmar after a devastating earthquake caused widespread destruction and loss of life.
 
• This operation was part of India’s commitment to providing humanitarian aid to its neighbors under its **"Neighborhood First" policy**.
 
• The assistance primarily included **rescue operations, medical aid, and relief supplies**, as Myanmar faced severe challenges due to the earthquake's aftermath.
 
• The operation was conducted with the support of Indian armed forces, medical teams, and disaster response units to ensure the swift delivery of aid.
 
• India has a history of supporting its neighbors during crises, reflecting its role as a responsible regional power and its strong bilateral ties with Myanmar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India-Myanmar Relations:**

 
 
• Myanmar shares a **1,643 km-long border** with India, touching four Indian states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram.
 
• India and Myanmar have close historical, cultural, and economic ties. Myanmar is a key partner in India’s **Act East Policy**.
 
• The two countries have collaborated on infrastructure projects such as the **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project** and the **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway**.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake in Myanmar (March 2025):**
 
 
• The earthquake caused significant damage to infrastructure, homes, and public services, displacing thousands of people.
 
• Many areas were left without basic necessities such as food, water, and medical care, prompting international humanitarian responses.
 
 
 
• **India’s Disaster Assistance Framework:**
 
 
• India has a robust disaster response mechanism led by organizations such as the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and the armed forces.
 
• India has previously launched similar missions like **Operation Maitri** to assist Nepal after the 2015 earthquake and **Operation Dost** to aid Turkey and Syria in 2023.
 
 
 
• **Neighborhood First Policy:**
 
 
• India’s Neighborhood First policy focuses on prioritizing relations with neighboring countries to ensure regional cooperation, stability, and development.
 
• Humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) operations are an integral part of this policy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operation Maitri (Nepal, 2015):**

 
 
• Conducted in response to the devastating earthquake in Nepal, providing rescue and relief operations.
 
• Included the deployment of the Indian Air Force and NDRF teams for search and rescue operations.
 
 
 
• **Operation Dost (Turkey and Syria, 2023):**
 
 
• India provided aid after the massive earthquake in Turkey and Syria, showcasing its commitment to global humanitarian efforts.
 
• Assistance included rescue teams, medical personnel, and essential supplies.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Response in India:**
 
 
• India has a comprehensive disaster response system led by the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and specialized agencies like the **NDRF**.
 
• India is recognized globally for its quick and efficient response to natural disasters in the region.

questions.question: Srinivasa Ramanujan, the mathematical genius, was passed away on April 26, 1920, at about what age?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**32**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• **Srinivasa Ramanujan**, one of the greatest mathematical geniuses, was born on **22 December 1887** in **Erode, Tamil Nadu, India**. 
• He passed away at the young age of **32 years** on **26 April 1920** due to health complications, primarily tuberculosis and related ailments. 
• Ramanujan made significant contributions to mathematical fields such as **number theory, continued fractions, and infinite series**, which remain influential in modern mathematics. 
• During his short life, he compiled nearly **3,900 mathematical results**, many of which were entirely original

questions.question: Who became the Chairman of ISRO in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**V. Narayanan**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **V. Narayanan** was appointed as the Chairman of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** in **January 2025**, succeeding the previous chairman. 
• He has been a notable figure in ISRO, previously serving as the **Director of the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)**, a critical division of ISRO responsible for developing liquid propulsion systems for launch vehicles and spacecraft. 
• V. Narayanan has been instrumental in India's space mission advancements, especially in areas like **cryogenic propulsion** and the development of **GSLV and GSLV Mk-III launch vehicles**. 
• His leadership is expected to further enhance ISRO's capabilities in satellite launches, interplanetary missions, and the development of newer technologies. 
• This appointment underscores his extensive contributions to India's space sector and his role in driving technological advancements. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):** 
• ISRO is the space agency of the Government of India, founded in **1969** by **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**. 
• Its headquarters is located in **Bengaluru, Karnataka**. 
• ISRO is known for its cost-effective space missions, including the **Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)** and the **Chandrayaan series**. 
• The organization focuses on satellite development, launch vehicle design, and interplanetary exploration. 
• **V. Narayanan's Contributions:** 
• He played a significant role in the development of **cryogenic engines** for ISRO's launch vehicles, including the **CE-20 engine** used in GSLV Mk-III. 
• Under his leadership, ISRO achieved milestones in **liquid propulsion technology** and enhanced the efficiency of India's space programs. 
• **Predecessors:** 
• **K. Sivan** (2018–2022): Known for spearheading the **Chandrayaan-2 mission** and the planning of **Gaganyaan**, India's human spaceflight program. 
• **S. Somanath** (2022–2025): Instrumental in advancing ISRO's launch vehicle capabilities and promoting international collaborations. 
• **Key ISRO Programs:** 
• **Chandrayaan Missions:** Focused on lunar exploration, including **Chandrayaan-3**. 
• **Gaganyaan:** India's first human spaceflight program, expected to launch in the near future. 
• **Satellite Launches:** Deployment of satellites for communication, navigation, and Earth observation. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **ISRO's Future Goals:** 
• Developing advanced launch vehicles like **Reusable Launch Vehicle (RLV)** to reduce launch costs. 
• Expanding India's presence in space exploration with missions to **Venus** and **deep space**. 
• Enhancing collaboration with international space agencies for joint missions and technology sharing. 
• **Global Recognition:** 
• ISRO is globally recognized for its **cost-effective space missions**, achieving significant milestones at a fraction of the cost compared to other space agencies. 
• The organization's success has positioned India as a key player in the global space industry. 
3e

questions.question: In November 2024, who has been appointed as Chief of BrahMos Aerospace?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaiteerth Raghavendra Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Jaiteerth Raghavendra Joshi** has been appointed as the Chief of **BrahMos Aerospace** in **November 2024**, succeeding the previous officeholder.

• **BrahMos Aerospace** is a joint venture between **India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and **Russia's NPO Mashinostroyenia (NPOM)**, known for developing the world-renowned supersonic cruise missile, BrahMos.

• Jaiteerth Raghavendra Joshi is an accomplished professional with expertise in **defense technology, strategic weapon systems, and management of aerospace projects**.

• The appointment of Joshi reflects India's strategic focus on modernizing its defense capabilities and strengthening its indigenous weapon systems production.

• Under his leadership, BrahMos Aerospace is expected to focus on **expanding its missile export markets** and developing advanced variants of the BrahMos missile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **BrahMos Missile:**

• The **BrahMos** is a **supersonic cruise missile** developed jointly by India and Russia, named after the rivers Brahmaputra (India) and Moskva (Russia).

• It has a speed of up to **Mach 3** (three times the speed of sound) and a range of **approximately 450–500 km**.

• It can be launched from various platforms including **land, sea, air, and underwater**, making it a versatile weapon system.

• It is capable of carrying conventional warheads and is known for its **precision strike capability**.

• **BrahMos Aerospace:**

• BrahMos Aerospace was established in **1998** as a joint venture between India's DRDO and Russia's NPOM.

• It aims to design, develop, produce, and market advanced missile systems for India and other friendly nations.

• The organization is headquartered in **New Delhi, India**.

• **India’s Focus on Defense Exports:**

• India has been actively promoting the export of BrahMos missiles to friendly countries such as **Philippines, Vietnam, and Indonesia**.

• In **2022**, India signed a deal with the Philippines to export BrahMos missiles worth **$375 million**.

• **Key Features of BrahMos Missile:**

• The missile employs **stealth technology** to evade radar detection and has a very low radar cross-section.

• It has **fire-and-forget capability**, meaning it does not require further guidance after launch.

• The missile is powered by a **solid propellant booster engine** and a liquid ramjet engine, ensuring high speed and range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Export Potential:** BrahMos has emerged as a key component of India's defense exports, with countries showing significant interest due to its **precision, versatility, and speed**.

• **Future Developments:** BrahMos Aerospace is working on **hypersonic variants** of the missile, which will have speeds exceeding **Mach 5**.

• **Strategic Importance:** The BrahMos missile enhances India's defense capabilities and acts as a **deterrent** against adversaries.

45

questions.question: In October 2024, who has been appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of Coal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram Dev Dutt**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Vikram Dev Dutt**, a senior bureaucrat from the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), was appointed as the **Secretary of the Ministry of Coal** in **October 2024**. 
• His appointment reflects his extensive experience in various administrative capacities and his ability to manage critical roles in government departments. 
• The **Ministry of Coal** is responsible for overseeing coal production, distribution, and policy formation in India, one of the major sectors contributing to energy and industrial growth. 
• Vikram Dev Dutt has previously held other significant positions, including being associated with the **Ministry of Tourism**, where he contributed to enhancing India's tourism sector. 
• The appointment of a seasoned IAS officer like Vikram Dev Dutt ensures administrative efficiency and robust policy execution in the coal sector. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Ministry of Coal:** 
• The **Ministry of Coal** was established in **1974** to develop and manage India's coal resources. 
• It oversees coal mining operations, formulates policies related to coal production, and ensures its sustainable use. 
• India is the **second-largest coal producer** globally, and coal contributes significantly to the nation's **energy sector**. 
• The ministry also focuses on promoting clean coal technologies and reducing environmental impacts. 
• **Role of the Secretary of Ministry of Coal:** 
• The Secretary of the Ministry of Coal is the administrative head of the ministry and is responsible for implementing government policies efficiently. 
• Key responsibilities include ensuring adequate coal supply to power plants, industries, and other sectors. 
• They also oversee the functioning of public sector undertakings like **Coal India Limited** and its subsidiaries. 
• Promoting sustainable mining practices and exploring renewable energy alternatives also form part of their responsibilities. 
• **Vikram Dev Dutt:** 
• A 1993-batch IAS officer of the **Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram-Union Territory (AGMUT) cadre**. 
• He has served in various roles, including as the **Chairman and Managing Director of Air India**, contributing to the aviation sector's growth. 
• Known for his administrative acumen, he has played pivotal roles in policy formulation and project implementation in different ministries. 
• **India's Coal Sector:** 
• Coal contributes to approximately **55% of India's energy needs**, making it a vital resource for industrial and economic growth. 
• Key producers of coal include **Coal India Limited**, which accounts for the majority of India's coal production. 
• India's coal reserves are concentrated in states like **Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and West Bengal**. 
• The government is working towards enhancing coal production and transitioning to **clean energy technologies** to meet future energy demands sustainably. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Coal India Limited:** 
• **Coal India Limited (CIL)** is the world's largest coal producer and a Maharatna company under the Ministry of Coal. 
• CIL operates through its subsidiaries and is responsible for producing and supplying coal to various sectors. 
• It has been instrumental in ensuring India's energy security and driving industrial growth. 
• **Clean Coal Technologies:** 
• To address environmental concerns, India is investing in **clean coal technologies**, such as carbon capture and storage (CCS). 
• Such technologies aim to reduce emissions from coal-based power plants and make coal usage more sustainable. 
• Government initiatives like **National Coal Gasification Mission** are promoting the use of coal gasification for cleaner energy production. </ul

questions.question: In Budget 2025, the Union Finance Minister announced to set up fifty thousand Atal Tinkering Labs in Government schools in next ________ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 5__** years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025**, the **Finance Minister** announced the establishment of **50,000 Atal Tinkering Labs** in government schools across India.
 
• The timeline for this ambitious project was set for completion within **5 years**, ensuring a systematic rollout and implementation of the labs.
 
• The initiative aims to foster a culture of **innovation, creativity, and scientific temperament** among school students by providing them access to state-of-the-art tools and technologies.
 
• **Atal Tinkering Labs** are part of the **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)**, launched by the Government of India to promote entrepreneurship and innovation at the grassroots level.
 
• The labs are equipped with advanced technologies such as **3D printers, robotics kits, sensors, and microcontrollers**, enabling students to work on **hands-on projects** and develop problem-solving skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM):**

 
 
• AIM is a flagship initiative by the **Government of India**, launched under the **NITI Aayog**, to promote innovation and entrepreneurship.
 
• It focuses on creating an ecosystem that supports **innovative ideas** and transforms them into viable solutions for societal challenges.
 
• AIM operates multiple programs, including **Atal Tinkering Labs**, **Atal Incubation Centers**, and **Mentor India Campaign**.
 
• The mission targets schools, colleges, startups, and MSMEs to build a robust innovation-driven economy.
 
 
 
• **Objective of Atal Tinkering Labs:**
 
 
• The labs aim to nurture students from **Classes VI to XII** by exposing them to **STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics)** concepts.
 
• The primary goal is to develop **critical thinking** and problem-solving skills in young minds.
 
• Such initiatives ensure India's readiness for the **Fourth Industrial Revolution**.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for Atal Tinkering Labs:**
 
 
• The program targets **Government and Government-aided schools**, ensuring inclusivity for underprivileged students.
 
• Schools are selected based on their proposals demonstrating a commitment to fostering an **innovation culture**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Atal Tinkering Labs:**
 
 
• Over the years, these labs have successfully inspired students to participate in **national and international competitions**.
 
• They have helped create a generation of **innovative thinkers** and potential future entrepreneurs.
 
• Real-life examples include students designing solutions for **environmental sustainability**, **healthcare challenges**, and **smart cities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budget 2025 Announcement:**

 
 
• The **Union Finance Minister** emphasized the role of **education and innovation** in driving India's economic growth.
 
• Allocations were made to expand access to innovation hubs like the **Atal Tinkering Labs**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Finland** and **Singapore** have adopted similar STEM-focused initiatives in schools, showing significant improvements in student innovation capabilities.
 
• India's investment in Atal Tinkering Labs positions it as a global leader in **grassroots innovation education**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Tools:**
 
 
• Labs are equipped with tools like **Arduino boards, Raspberry Pi kits**, and **IoT devices**, enabling students to explore modern technologies.
 
• Such tools help students understand concepts like **coding, robotics, and machine learning** from an early age.

questions.question: SATAT initiative seen in news in November 2024 is related to which union ministry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **SATAT initiative** (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) is spearheaded by the **Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas**.

• It was launched in **October 2018** to promote the use of **Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG)** as a clean and affordable alternative fuel for transportation.

• The objective of the initiative is to boost the production of **Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG)** from various waste and biomass sources like agricultural residue, municipal solid waste, sugarcane press mud, and cattle dung.

• SATAT is aimed at reducing dependency on **fossil fuels**, addressing environmental concerns, and increasing farmer income by utilizing agricultural residue.

• The initiative also supports the government's vision of a **"Swachh Bharat" (Clean India)** by addressing the issue of organic waste management effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG):**

• CBG is a purified version of biogas, which has properties similar to compressed natural gas (**CNG**).

• It can be used as a fuel for vehicles and has a calorific value of approximately 52,000 KJ/kg.

• CBG is produced through the **anaerobic digestion** of biomass and waste materials, ensuring efficient waste utilization.

• CBG can be transported through cylinders or pipelines and used for cooking, industrial purposes, and as automotive fuel.

• **Benefits of SATAT Initiative:**

• It helps in reducing **carbon emissions** by replacing fossil fuels with a cleaner alternative.

• Promotes effective **waste management** by utilizing organic waste for energy production.

• Creates job opportunities in rural areas, especially in the collection and processing of biomass.

• Enhances **energy security** by reducing dependency on imported crude oil.

• **Stakeholders Involved:**

• Public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) like **Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL)** are key players in implementing the SATAT initiative.

• Private sector participation is encouraged to set up **CBG production plants** and supply chains.

• **Government Goals:**

• The SATAT initiative aligns with India’s target of achieving **Net Zero emissions by 2070**.

• The government aims to establish **5,000 CBG plants** across the country by 2025, with a production capacity of 15 million metric tonnes annually.

• It contributes to achieving the goals of the **National Policy on Biofuels**, which emphasizes the production of alternative fuels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Other Ministries:**

• **Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs:** Focuses on urban development schemes like Smart Cities Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission.

• **Ministry of Urban Development:** Now merged with the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs.

• **Ministry of Home Affairs:** Handles internal security, disaster management, and law enforcement.

• **Achievements of SATAT:**

• Several CBG production plants have been commissioned under SATAT, generating employment and contributing to cleaner energy.

• The initiative has garnered interest from private players, leading to investments in bio-energy infrastructure.

questions.question: In Cricket, a _____________ will be declared if the umpire thinks the batsman did not have a reasonable opportunity to score off the deliver.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wide Ball**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• A **Wide Ball** is declared in cricket when the umpire judges that the bowler has delivered the ball too far away from the batsman, making it difficult or impossible for the batsman to play a legitimate shot. 

• The rule governing a **Wide Ball** ensures that the bowler delivers the ball within a region where the batsman has a reasonable opportunity to score runs. 

• If the ball passes on the leg side of the batsman or is significantly wide of the off stump, it may be adjudged as a **Wide Ball**, unless the batsman moves to make contact with the ball. 

• A **Wide Ball** results in one run being added to the batting team's score, and the delivery does not count towards the bowler's over. 

• The umpire signals a **Wide Ball** by extending both arms horizontally. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Wide Ball Rule:** 

• A **Wide Ball** is part of the **Laws of Cricket**, specifically under Law 22, which governs the criteria for declaring a ball as "wide."

• The rule is meant to ensure fairness and competitiveness in the game, allowing batsmen a reasonable chance to play the ball.

• The ball must pass within a certain area on either side of the stumps to be considered a legitimate delivery.

• **Impact of Wide Ball:** 

• It adds an extra run to the batting team's total score.

• The extra delivery ensures the batting side gets more opportunities to score.

• It is considered a mistake by the bowler and adds pressure by increasing the number of deliveries in an over.

• **Comparison with Other Deliveries:** 

• **Fast Ball:** Refers to a delivery bowled at high speed. It is legitimate unless it breaches other rules (e.g., height restrictions).

• **Yorker:** A ball aimed at the batsman's feet, often used to restrict scoring opportunities. It cannot be a Wide Ball unless misdirected.

• **Length Ball:** Refers to balls pitched at a specific distance from the batsman. These are legitimate unless they stray wide.

• **Umpire's Judgment:** 

• The umpire's role is critical in determining whether a ball is wide. Their decision is based on the batsman's stance and movement.

• Technological aids like the Decision Review System (DRS) are not typically used for Wide Ball decisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Wide Ball in Limited Overs Cricket:** 

• In formats like **ODIs** and **T20s**, stricter rules apply for Wide Balls, especially on the leg side.

• Bowling wides can significantly impact the game by giving away extra runs and disrupting the bowler's rhythm.

• **Penalties for Wides:** 

• Each Wide Ball results in one penalty run for the bowling team.

• Repeated wides can lead to extra pressure and loss of control in critical game situations.

• **Examples:** 

• During the **2019 ICC Cricket World Cup**, wides were a major factor in teams' strategies and scores.

• In many matches, wides have led to close finishes, emphasizing the importance of disciplined bowling.

</ul

questions.question: In Track and Field Events, 800 meters and 1500 meters are of which type of race?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Middle/long**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Middle/long-distance races** refer to track events that range from 800 meters to 10,000 meters. These events test both speed and endurance.
 
• The **800 meters** race is considered a middle-distance event, requiring a combination of sprinting ability and aerobic endurance.
 
• The **1500 meters** race, often called the "metric mile," is another middle-distance event where athletes need strategic pacing and stamina.
 
• Both races are conducted on a **400-meter standard track**, with 800 meters requiring two laps and 1500 meters requiring three and three-quarters laps.
 
• These events are part of the **Olympic Games** and other international track and field championships, showcasing athletes' ability to balance speed and endurance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Middle/Long-Distance Races:**

 
 
• Middle-distance races, like 800 meters and 1500 meters, require a **balance between anaerobic and aerobic energy systems**.
 
• Strategies such as **pacing** and **positioning** play a significant role in these races.
 
• These events often involve a **final sprint** in the last 100-200 meters to secure victory.
 
 
 
• **Training for Middle-Distance Events:**
 
 
• Athletes train to enhance their **VO2 max** (aerobic capacity) and **lactate threshold** for sustained performance.
 
• Workouts include a mix of **interval training**, **long runs**, and **speed drills**.
 
 
 
• **Notable Records:**
 
 
• The **world record** for 800 meters (as of 2023) is held by **David Rudisha** of Kenya, with a time of 1:40.91 set in 2012.
 
• The **world record** for 1500 meters (as of 2023) is held by **Hicham El Guerrouj** of Morocco, with a time of 3:26.00 set in 1998.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Race Types:**
 
 
• **Sprints:** Events like 100m and 200m that rely purely on anaerobic energy and explosive power.
 
• **Hurdles:** Races like 110m hurdles where athletes jump over barriers while maintaining speed.
 
• **Road Running:** Includes marathons and half-marathons conducted on roads, requiring high endurance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** Middle/long-distance events have been a part of the **Olympic Games** since their inception in 1896.
 
• **Physiological Demands:** Athletes require a mix of **fast-twitch** and **slow-twitch muscle fibers** to excel in these races.
 
• **Famous Athletes:** Legends like **Paavo Nurmi**, **Sebastian Coe**, and **Faith Kipyegon** have excelled in these events, earning global recognition.

questions.question: As of 31 July 2025, who holds the record for most Asian Games medals by an Indian athlete?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PT Usha**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **PT Usha**, often referred to as the "Queen of Indian Track and Field," holds the record for the most **Asian Games medals by an Indian athlete**. 
• She won a total of **11 medals** at the **Asian Games**, including 4 gold medals, 7 silver medals, and no bronze medals. 
• Her performance at the **1986 Seoul Asian Games** was particularly remarkable, where she won 4 golds and 1 silver in track and field events.

questions.question: In Cricket, a wide ball will add how many run/s to the batting team?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 run**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In the game of **cricket**, when a bowler bowls a delivery that is deemed too wide for the batsman to reach and play a legitimate shot, it is called a **wide ball**. 
• A wide ball is signaled by the umpire by stretching both arms horizontally. **The batting team is awarded 1 run for every wide ball bowled.** 
• Additionally, if the wicketkeeper or fielders fail to stop the ball, the batting team can score extra runs called **"byes"** on the wide delivery. 
• A wide ball also adds to the bowler's tally of **extra deliveries**, meaning the bowler has to bowl another legal delivery to complete the over. 
• The 1 run awarded for a wide ball is added to the **team's total score** but not to the batsman's individual score. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Wide Ball in Cricket:** 
• A ball is considered wide if it is bowled outside the reach of the batsman on either the off-side or leg-side of the pitch, making it impossible for the batsman to play a normal shot. 
• This rule ensures that bowlers maintain a fair and competitive line and length during the game. 
• **Penalty Runs:** 
• A wide ball contributes to the **extras** in the match, which include wides, no-balls, byes, and leg-byes. 
• Extras are crucial in close matches and can significantly impact the outcome of the game. 
• **Impact on Bowling Statistics:** 
• Wide balls count as **penalty deliveries** and are added to the bowler's tally of balls bowled, but they do not count as legitimate deliveries. 
• This can negatively affect the bowler's **economy rate** in the game. 
• **Examples in Matches:** 
• Wide balls have often been a deciding factor in **limited-overs cricket**, especially in tight games where every run counts. 
• For instance, in the **2019 Cricket World Cup final**, extras like wides played a key role in the final score. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **ICC Rules:** The rules regarding wides are defined by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)** and are followed in all international and domestic matches. 
• **Wide in Different Formats:** The interpretation of a wide ball can vary slightly in **different formats** of the game, such as Test matches, ODIs, and T20s. 
• **No-Ball vs. Wide Ball:** While both result in extra runs, a **no-ball** also allows a **free-hit** in limited-overs cricket, whereas a wide ball does not. </ul

questions.question: In which year was the fixed rate repos in government securities was introduced to give maneuverability in liquidity management?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **fixed-rate repos** in government securities were introduced in **1997** to enhance the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) ability to manage liquidity effectively. 
• This mechanism allowed the RBI to inject or absorb liquidity from the banking system by conducting repo operations at a predetermined fixed rate. 
• The primary objective was to ensure stability in the **money market** and to provide banks with a reliable tool for short-term borrowing or lending. 
• The introduction of fixed-rate repos was a significant step in modernizing India's monetary policy framework and aligning it with global practices. 
• Fixed-rate repos contributed to better **interest rate transmission**, which helped the RBI in implementing its monetary policy more efficiently. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Repo Rate:** 
• The repo rate is the **rate at which the RBI lends money** to commercial banks against government securities. 
• It is a key monetary policy tool used to control inflation and regulate liquidity in the economy. 
• Changes in the repo rate directly affect borrowing costs for banks and subsequently influence lending rates for consumers and businesses. 
• **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF):** 
• The LAF was introduced by the RBI in **2000** as part of its monetary policy reforms. 
• It comprises repo and reverse repo operations to manage liquidity in the banking system. 
• While fixed-rate repos were introduced earlier in 1997, the LAF institutionalized their use alongside reverse repos to create a comprehensive framework. 
• **Impact of Fixed-Rate Repos:** 
• Improved the predictability and stability of liquidity management. 
• Enhanced transparency in monetary policy operations by providing a clear signal to the market. 
• Supported the development of a more robust and efficient **government securities market**. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The introduction of fixed-rate repos came during a period of significant financial reforms in India, including the liberalization of the economy in the 1990s. 
• These reforms aimed to modernize India's financial sector and integrate it with global markets. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate:** 
• The reverse repo rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks. 
• It is used to absorb excess liquidity in the banking system and is typically lower than the repo rate. 
• **Government Securities:** 
• These are debt instruments issued by the government to finance its fiscal deficit. 
• They are considered safe investments due to the government's backing and are used in repo transactions. 
• **Monetary Policy Transmission:** 
• The effectiveness of repo and reverse repo rates depends on how well they are transmitted to the broader economy. 
• Efficient transmission ensures that changes in policy rates influence market rates, inflation, and economic growth. </ul

questions.question: As per census 2001, what was the sex ratio of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**933**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sex ratio** is defined as the number of females per 1,000 males in a population. It is a critical demographic indicator that reflects the social and economic conditions of a society.
 
• As per the **Census 2001**, the sex ratio of India was **933 females per 1,000 males**. This was an improvement from the sex ratio of **927** recorded in the **Census 1991**.
 
• The sex ratio in India varies significantly across states and regions. For instance, states like **Kerala** reported a higher sex ratio of **1,058**, while states like **Haryana** recorded much lower figures at **861**.
 
• The improvement in the overall sex ratio in 2001 can be attributed to increased awareness about gender equality and various government initiatives aimed at reducing gender disparities.
 
• The sex ratio is an important measure for policymakers as it highlights issues related to gender equity, female mortality, and the impact of social practices like preference for male children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Terminologies:**

 
 
• **Sex Ratio:** The number of females per 1,000 males in a population.
 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):** The sex ratio among children aged 0-6 years. In Census 2001, the CSR was **927**, indicating a preference for male children in society.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations:**
 
 
• **Kerala:** Known for its high literacy rates and progressive social indicators, it had the highest sex ratio of **1,058** in 2001.
 
• **Haryana:** This state recorded one of the lowest sex ratios, highlighting issues like **female infanticide** and **gender bias**.
 
• **National Capital Territory (Delhi):** Reported a sex ratio of only **821**, indicating urban challenges in gender equity.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing the Sex Ratio:**
 
 
• **Social Practices:** Practices like **female infanticide**, **dowry system**, and preference for male children heavily skew the sex ratio.
 
• **Economic Factors:** In rural areas, male children are often seen as assets for farming, while females are perceived as financial burdens.
 
• **Healthcare:** Lack of access to healthcare for women, especially during pregnancy and childbirth, contributes to higher female mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** scheme launched in **2015** aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote gender equality.
 
• The **Janani Suraksha Yojana** focuses on reducing maternal and infant mortality by promoting institutional deliveries.
 
• Awareness campaigns and stricter enforcement of the **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, 1994**, which prohibits sex determination tests, have been implemented to combat gender-based sex selection.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison:**
 
 
• The global average sex ratio at birth is around **952 females per 1,000 males**. India’s overall sex ratio in 2001 was below this global average.
 
• Countries like **China** and **Pakistan** also face similar challenges with skewed sex ratios due to cultural preferences for male children.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The improvement in the sex ratio from 927 in 1991 to **933** in 2001 was a significant milestone, reflecting a gradual shift in societal attitudes towards gender equality.
 
• The **child sex ratio** remains a critical area of concern, as it reflects deep-rooted gender biases and the prevalence of practices like **female foeticide**.
 
• Efforts to improve the sex ratio must focus on a multi-pronged approach, including **education**, **awareness campaigns**, and **strict enforcement** of laws against gender discrimination.

questions.question: In the context of economy, if __________ is deducted from the gross value added to obtain the Net value added obtained.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Depreciation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Gross Value Added (GVA)** measures the total value of goods and services produced in an economy before accounting for depreciation or capital consumption.

• When **Depreciation** (also known as capital consumption) is subtracted from GVA, the resulting value is **Net Value Added (NVA).**

• **Depreciation** refers to the decrease in the value of capital assets (like machinery, buildings, etc.) over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or usage.

• This deduction is crucial as it reflects the actual net output or production of an economy by excluding the value lost due to asset degradation.

• In the calculation of NVA, other components like taxes, subsidies, wages, etc., are not directly subtracted from GVA but are considered under different accounting measures. ***Hence, Depreciation is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Gross Value Added (GVA):**

• **GVA** is a measure of economic productivity, showing the value of output less intermediate consumption.

• It is used to assess the contribution of various sectors to the overall economic activity of a country.

• GVA is a critical indicator for policymakers to understand sectoral performance and plan interventions accordingly.

• **Net Value Added (NVA):**

• **NVA** is derived by subtracting depreciation from the Gross Value Added.

• It represents the true economic value created by an economy, excluding the cost of maintaining and replacing capital assets.

• NVA is used to understand the net productivity and efficiency of an economy.

• **Depreciation:**

• Depreciation is the systematic reduction in the value of an asset over its useful life.

• It accounts for wear and tear, obsolescence, and usage, ensuring accurate financial representation of assets.

• Methods to calculate depreciation include **straight-line method**, **declining balance method**, and **units of production method**.

• **Other Components in Economic Accounting:**

• **Net Indirect Tax:** It represents the difference between indirect taxes and subsidies and is added to NVA to calculate GDP at market prices.

• **Subsidy:** A financial aid provided by the government to reduce the cost of goods or services, influencing the overall economic calculation.

• **Wages:** Payments made to labor, which are part of the compensation of employees but not deducted from GVA directly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):**

• GDP at market prices is calculated by adding **Net Indirect Taxes** to **GVA at factor cost.**

• It provides a comprehensive measure of economic activity, including taxes and subsidies on products.

• **Economic Accounting Systems:**

• National accounts use measures like GVA, NVA, and GDP to assess economic performance.

• These metrics are essential for policy formulation, economic planning, and international comparisons.

• **Application of Depreciation:**

• Depreciation is crucial in corporate accounting for tax benefits and accurate financial reporting.

• It ensures businesses set aside resources for asset replacement, maintaining operational efficiency.

</ul

questions.question: On the banks of which river was the Harappan site of 'Harappa' discovered in 1920-22?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi River**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• The Harappan site of **Harappa** was discovered on the banks of the **Ravi River** during the excavations conducted between **1920-22** by archaeologists under the leadership of **Sir John Marshall**, Rai Bahadur Daya Ram Sahni, and others. 
• **Harappa** is one of the most significant archaeological sites of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, showcasing a highly developed urban settlement of the Bronze Age. 
• The site is located in present-day **Sahiwal district, Punjab, Pakistan**. The Ravi River played a crucial role in the establishment and sustenance of the settlement by providing water resources and facilitating trade and agriculture. 
• The discovery of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro led to the identification of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, also known as the **Harappan Civilization**, which dates back to approximately **3300 BCE to 1300 BCE**. 
• The findings at Harappa include granaries, wells, drainage systems, seals, terracotta figurines, and evidence of trade networks, suggesting a sophisticated and organized urban lifestyle.
